newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Gurkhas win gruelling HK trail walk for last time.
newsitem.headline: Gurkhas win gruelling HK trail walk for last time.

text.p: A team of British Gurkha soldiers won a 100 km trail walk in Hong Kong on Saturday for the last time before the colony reverts to China next year.
The four-man Queen's Gurkha Signal team crossed the finish line 13 hours 28 minutes after the start, but was 10 minutes short of breaking the record set by another Gurkha team in 1993.
The event, sponsored by the Queen's Gurkha Signals and Oxfam Hong Kong, attracted 700 teams with a record 2,800 runners.
The walk is expected to raise HK$13 million (US$1.68 million) for Oxfam, the Gurkha Welfare Trust and local charities working with the disabled.
British troops stationed in Hong Kong will leave the colony at midnight next June 30 when the territory reverts to Beijing's rule.

The Gurkhas -- Nepali soldiers known for their hardiness, loyalty and combat skills -- bade a ceremonial farewell to the territory earlier this month. The last Gurkha infantry battalion will leave the colony in stages over November and December.
The Queen's Gurkha Signals' Sergeant-Major Om Gurung told the Hong Kong Standard it was a sad occasion.
"For most people this is just fun run. But for all Gurkhas the MacLehose Trail is our training ground, part of our normal fitness exercise," he said.
